plan: Given my value is $9, I need to balance winning with not overpaying. Since this is the first and only round, I don't have historical data to analyze other bidders' tendencies. A common strategy in second-price auctions is to bid your true value. However, with two other rational bidders, they might also bid their value or slightly below. Bidding my value ensures I win if my value is the highest, and I never pay more than my value. I will bid my value to maximize profit in this single round.

My value is $9. This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with payment equal to the second-highest bid. This is effectively a Vickrey auction. In a Vickrey auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes my profit regardless of what other bidders do.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes your expected utility regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding below your value risks losing a profitable item, while bidding above your value risks winning an item for more than it's worth.
